newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee ends flat on high dlr supply.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee ends flat on high dlr supply.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed virtually unmoved against the dollar on Monday due to an oversupply of greenbacks in the market, dealers said.
The rupee closed at its opening level of 58.48, hovering near the Central Bank's buying range. On Friday, the rupee closed at 58.49.
"It was a very lethargic trading day. There were some import covering, but inward remittances outstrip imports these days," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer.
Dealers said money was coming in mostly for investment in the country's stock market, which has tilted the balance more towards inward remittances.
"There are plenty of dollars in the market, which has reduced the demand for the U.S. currency," a local bank dealer said.
Dealers said the dollar-rupee exchange rate should remain at current levels, unless there was a large import bill.
The Central Bank pushed the dollar down by 0.25 local cents and fixed buying and selling rates at 58.4744 and 59.6557 respectively.
Overnight call money, which opened at 9.75 percent, closed 9.5 percent with the market highly liquid.
